title: Overcoming Production Bottlenecks with Smart Automation and AI Solutions
summary: If your business doesn't adopt automation and AI, and soon, it simply won't be able to compete or survive.
body_text: Production bottlenecks, regardless of their place in the supply chain, inhibit businesses from maintaining efficiency and meeting consumer demand. In the cannabis industry, these moments of congestion are frustrating. But more importantly, they slow down production and lead to significant expenses. What can be done about it? Smart automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven solutions can address and rectify these bottlenecks. Advanced technologies, such as robotics and computer vision, can help reduce downtime across production lines in the cannabis space. According to SilverLeaf's State of the Cannabis Industry report for 2024 , 40% of respondents report they plan to increase the use of automation and robotics for production to enhance operational efficiency. Which comes as no surprise as the report also states over 80% of survey respondents plan to leverage automation technology to streamline processes and reduce costs. Meanwhile, 58.5% believe manufacturing and production processes are among the most significant areas ripe for this type of advancement in technology. Common Production Bottlenecks Cannabis Manufacturers Face Today A bottleneck in manufacturing is typically defined as any point where materials accumulate or get stuck. Bottlenecks can shift along an assembly line depending on how efficiently the line is running . For example, if you start from scratch, the bottleneck might be in one area, such as infusing pre-rolls, but once you improve that, it could shift a few stages down the line to, let's say, packaging the pre-rolls into tubes. Then, if you address that, the bottleneck could move somewhere else, or even back to the beginning of the process. It all depends on where things are slowing down. When I think about bottlenecks, I focus on where the most labor is concentrated . In the cannabis industry, labor often becomes concentrated in certain areas, like making hash holes or rolling kief-coated joints, which require a lot of manual work. However, one consistent issue across the board , regardless of the specific product, is final packaging—getting pre-rolls into tubes, bags, or jars. This is where I've seen most hold-ups occur. And let's not forget about quality control. Quality control at scale is another big issue, whether we're talking about pre-rolls, eighth jars, concentrate jars, or cartridges. There's no standardized method for quality control across the industry and this nuanced process often halts the flow of production. How Can Automation and AI Solutions Address Production Bottlenecks? 1. Increasing Throughput and Reducing Labor Dependencies When it comes to infusing pre-rolls or packaging products into their final containers, automation mitigates the reliance on manual labor. This enables production lines to accelerate output while reducing labor costs and eliminating human error. For example, a business that uses automation to infuse or coat pre-rolls will achieve a higher output at a lower cost without needing to hire additional workers. Plus, this automation frees up workers to engage in more value-adding tasks, helping to increase production and the company's bottom line. 2. Optimizing Space Utilization Some businesses have maxed out the efficiency they can achieve within their current square footage. Expanding their space would likely require a significant investment, often adding up to millions of dollars. So, to increase their output, they have to optimize every square foot of their current facility. Automation enables businesses to achieve higher production density by increasing speed and throughput in smaller spaces without sacrificing said space for dozens of workers on knock boxes. 3. Enhancing Quality Control with AI Right now, humans are involved in every part of quality control because there's no other viable alternative. However, computer vision, an AI-driven solution, is a promising resolution to quality control bottlenecks. In theory , it can be used for real-time quality control, meaning humans wouldn't need to check every product. AI can standardize quality control (even when regulations vary by product and state) ensuring quality consistency across products and state lines. 4. Automating the Final Packaging Stage Tubes, bags, jars—all this variability in final packaging makes the process cumbersome and slow for manual laborers. Yet, with automation, especially the kind powered by AI to adapt to different packaging types, can ensure final packaging is quick, consistent, and of the utmost quality. 5. Minimizing Production Downtime Often, it's the unexpected breakdowns or machine failures that lead to delays in production . AI algorithms can enable predictive maintenance to prevent machine downtimes, ensuring consistent and smooth operations. 6. Scaling Without Increased Labor Costs As businesses grow, they often reduce manual labor with AI, but there's a concern that pulling people out of the process can reduce quality. However, AI-driven solutions can actually improve quality control, ensuring consistent, even superior , results. In fact, implementing AI solutions enables companies to reallocate labor strategically to further check quality and consistency, which increases brand equity. Scaling from a small team of five to a workforce of 50 or 100 can be an operational and HR challenge. However, with automation and AI, scaling from , say, 10 units of production to 100 becomes far more manageable—what would have been a 7 out of 10 in difficulty with a manual workforce might only be a 3 out of 10 with automation. Stardust from Sorting Robotics is an automated, kief-coating robot. Sorting Robotics The Future of Automation and AI in Cannabis The sophistication of cannabis businesses' full manufacturing line is going to change within the next five years, as I believe the entire industry will be automated. Currently, about half of the industry is automated. In the coming years, and especially if cannabis is rescheduled to a Schedule III substance , compliance needs and market demands are going to drive the requirement for efficiency, which, in turn, is going to necessitate automation. And let's be clear: bottlenecks are only the beginning of why cannabis leaders are automating processes throughout their supply chain. As more brands expand into new markets, consistency is vita l— a utomation ensures this never falters. If your business doesn't adopt automation and AI, and soon, it simply won't be able to compete or survive. The automated kief-coating robot, Stardust, from Sorting Robotics. Sorting Robotics About the Author Nohtal Partansky is the founder and CEO of Sorting Robotics. He is a serial entrepreneur and former NASA-JPL engineer. At NASA-JPL, Partansky was a cognizant engineer on the MOXIE project ; an instrument on the surface of Mars producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere. After leaving NASA-JPL, Partansky founded Sorting Robotics with his co-founder, Cassio Dos Santos Jr. Since the company's inception, Partansky has led Sorting Robotics in building innovative equipment for cannabis manufacturers and vertically integrated brands. While building Sorting Robotics, he witnessed firsthand how the lack of automation in the cannabis industry disrupts the value chain and erodes profit margins. Today, Sorting Robotics is working to solve those problems with AI-driven machines deployed across North America.

title: Top 8 Time Blocking Tips to Boost Your Productivity - Sunsama Blog
summary: Discover essential time blocking tips to optimize your daily schedule. Improve your workflow and achieve more.
body_text: Taming Your Time: A Guide to Effective Time Blocking Are you a busy professional seeking practical time blocking tips to boost your productivity? Do you want to integrate time blocking seamlessly with Sunsama for enhanced workflow management? This listicle offers eight actionable strategies to optimize your daily schedule and achieve peak performance. Learn how to structure your time effectively, minimize distractions, and conquer your to-do list with these targeted time blocking techniques. Time blocking, when done right, empowers you to take control of your day. It's a proactive approach to time management that moves beyond simply scheduling appointments. These time blocking tips will provide specific strategies to maximize your focus and achieve your goals, especially when integrated with a platform like Sunsama. We'll explore practical methods to implement time blocking, covering everything from structuring individual blocks to reviewing your progress. This isn't about generic advice - these are focused, actionable insights designed for ambitious professionals. You will learn to: Structure your day for maximum focus: Discover the power of small time blocks and how to batch similar tasks. Integrate self-care: See why allocating specific blocks for personal activities is crucial for long-term productivity. Leverage Sunsama effectively: Understand how these time blocking tips can enhance your workflow within the Sunsama platform. Dynamically adjust your schedule: Learn how to review and adapt your time blocks for continuous improvement. Stop merely reacting to your workday and start proactively shaping it. Let's dive into these powerful time blocking tips. 1. Start with Small Time Blocks One of the biggest hurdles to successful time blocking is the feeling of being overwhelmed. Trying to structure every minute of your day from the outset can be daunting and often leads to abandoning the system altogether. A gentler, more effective approach is to start with small, manageable time blocks. Instead of scheduling hour-long blocks, begin with increments of 15-30 minutes. This allows you to acclimate to the practice and experience small wins, building momentum and confidence in the process. It's about building a habit, not overhauling your entire workflow overnight. Screenshot of small timeblocks on a calendar in Sunsama Examples of Small Time Blocks Email Management: Block 20 minutes to process incoming emails and respond to urgent messages. Break Time: Schedule 15-minute breaks between meetings to recharge and avoid burnout. This allows you to transition more effectively and return to work refreshed. Daily Planning: Allocate 30 minutes each morning to review your schedule, prioritize tasks, and time block your day. Actionable Tips for Implementation Use a Timer: Set a timer—like the one in Sunsama —for your allocated time block to create a sense of urgency and stay focused. Gradual Increase: As you become comfortable with shorter blocks, gradually increase their duration. This allows you to find the optimal time block length for your specific work style and tasks. Track Your Success: Monitor your ability to stay within your allocated time blocks. This data provides valuable insights and reinforces positive behavior. Start Small: Begin with just 2-3 time blocks per day. Focus on mastering these before expanding to encompass more of your schedule. Why Start Small? For busy professionals, particularly tech workers, consultants, entrepreneurs, and CEOs, time is a precious commodity. Time blocking offers a powerful way to regain control of your schedule and increase productivity. However, the initial transition can be challenging. Starting with small time blocks makes the process less intimidating and more sustainable, increasing the likelihood of long-term success. This approach is especially beneficial for those new to time blocking or those who have previously struggled with implementing the technique. It allows you to experience the benefits of time blocking without feeling overwhelmed, paving the way for a more structured and productive workflow. This strategy deserves its place in this list because it provides a practical entry point for anyone looking to optimize their time management using tools like Sunsama. 2. Batch Similar Tasks Together One of the most effective time blocking strategies is batching similar tasks together. This technique involves grouping related activities into dedicated time blocks, minimizing context switching and maximizing focus. By concentrating on one type of work at a time, you leverage the power of deep work, allowing your brain to operate more efficiently and produce higher-quality output. This approach is particularly beneficial for complex projects or tasks requiring significant mental effort. Examples of Task Batching Communication Blitz: Dedicate a 2-hour block each morning to handle all emails, phone calls, and instant messages. Content Creation Power Hour: Set aside Tuesday afternoons specifically for writing, editing, and scheduling social media posts. Friday Admin Focus: Reserve Friday mornings to process invoices, expense reports, and other administrative tasks. Client Meeting Days: Group all client meetings on Mondays and Wednesdays to free up other days for deep work. Actionable Tips for Implementation Identify Task Types: Start by listing your most common task types. This will help you visualize potential batching opportunities. Peak Performance Batching: Schedule your batching sessions during your peak energy times for optimal productivity. Thematic Days: Consider implementing themed days, such as "Meeting Monday" or "Creative Thursday", to further streamline your workflow. Running Task List: Maintain a running list of tasks you can batch together. This will help you quickly populate your time blocks. Why Batch Similar Tasks? For busy professionals like tech workers, consultants, and entrepreneurs, context switching is a major productivity drain. Batching similar tasks reduces this friction, allowing you to enter a flow state and accomplish more in less time. Learn more about task batching to refine your approach. This strategy deserves a spot on this list because it provides a practical and efficient way to optimize your workflow and maximize your output. Using a platform like Sunsama, you can easily implement task batching and experience its powerful benefits. This is a powerful technique for anyone looking to regain control of their schedule and enhance their productivity. 3. Build in Buffer Time One of the biggest pitfalls of time blocking is the assumption that everything will go exactly as planned. Meetings run late, urgent requests pop up, and tasks often take longer than anticipated. To prevent your carefully crafted schedule from collapsing, intentionally incorporate buffer time between your time blocks. This protective layer of unscheduled time allows you to absorb unexpected delays and transitions without derailing your entire day. Even a small buffer of 10-15 minutes can make a significant difference. Examples of Buffer Time Meeting Gaps: Schedule 15-minute gaps between back-to-back meetings to account for overruns and allow time to prepare for the next meeting. Presentation Prep: Include a buffer before important presentations to review your materials, compose yourself, and address any last-minute technical issues. Work Transitions: Build in transition periods between deep work sessions and collaborative tasks to mentally shift gears and maintain focus. End-of-Day Buffer: Allocate time at the end of the day for wrap-up activities, such as reviewing emails, organizing your workspace, and planning for the next day. Actionable Tips for Implementation Start with 15 Minutes: Begin with 15-minute buffers and adjust the duration based on your experience and the specific demands of your work. Utilize for Quick Tasks: Use buffer time for small, manageable tasks like checking emails, responding to messages, or organizing your to-do list. Keep Buffers Clear: Resist the urge to schedule tasks during buffer periods. These are designed as safety nets, not additional work slots. Track Buffer Usage: Monitor how often you actually need the buffer time. This data will help you optimize buffer duration for maximum efficiency. Why Build in Buffer Time? Time blocking is a powerful productivity tool for ambitious professionals, especially those in demanding roles like tech workers, consultants, entrepreneurs, and CEOs. However, life rarely adheres to rigid schedules. Buffer time provides flexibility and resilience, ensuring that unexpected interruptions don't domino into a day of missed deadlines and unmet goals. This strategy enhances the effectiveness of time blocking by acknowledging the unpredictable nature of work, making it a crucial component of any successful time management system. By incorporating buffer time, professionals can enhance their productivity and peace of mind, making this a valuable time blocking tip for those seeking to optimize their workflow using tools like Sunsama. 4. Match Tasks to Energy Levels One of the most effective time blocking tips revolves around understanding and leveraging your natural energy rhythms. This means aligning your most demanding tasks with your peak energy periods, while scheduling less intensive activities for times when your energy naturally dips. This chronotype-based approach, popularized by author Daniel Pink and high-performance coaches, allows you to work with your biology, not against it, for maximum productivity. Examples of Matching Tasks to Energy Peak Performance: Schedule deep work, creative brainstorming, or important client meetings during your high-energy hours. For many, this is the morning. Post-Lunch Dip: Reserve the post-lunch dip for routine tasks like email management, organizing files, or catching up on industry news. Afternoon Slump: If you experience an afternoon slump, use this time for less demanding activities or schedule a short break to recharge. Actionable Tips for Implementation Track Your Energy: Monitor your energy levels hourly for 1-2 weeks to identify your peak and low periods. Protect Your Peak: Treat your peak hours as sacred time. Guard them against distractions and low-value activities. Communicate Clearly: Inform colleagues about your optimal meeting times to ensure productive collaborations. Plan for Dips: Proactively schedule lighter tasks, like checking emails or organizing your to-do list, during your natural energy dips. Learn more about... Why Match Tasks to Energy Levels? This time blocking tip recognizes that productivity isn't about brute force; it's about working smarter. By syncing your tasks with your natural energy flow, you optimize your focus and output. This is especially crucial for busy professionals like tech workers, consultants, and entrepreneurs who juggle multiple demanding projects. Matching tasks to energy levels prevents burnout, maximizes efficiency, and leads to more consistent, high-quality work. This strategy is essential for any time blocking system, particularly when using a tool like Sunsama, which allows for detailed scheduling and task management. It elevates time blocking from a simple scheduling technique to a powerful strategy for optimizing performance. 5. Use Color Coding and Visual Systems One of the most effective ways to enhance your time blocking system is through visual organization. Implementing a system of color coding, symbols, or categories allows you to quickly differentiate between various types of time blocks at a glance. This visual approach minimizes cognitive load when reviewing your schedule, facilitating better comprehension and management of your daily activities. It also contributes to maintaining healthier work-life boundaries. Screenshot of Ashutosh Priyadarshy’s ideal calendar in Sunsama Examples of Visual Systems Color-Coded Categories: Blue for deep work, red for meetings, and green for personal time. Client or Project Differentiation: Assign unique colors to different clients or projects for easy identification. Task Types: Use patterns or symbols to distinguish between recurring tasks and one-time events. Intensity Levels: Represent the intensity or priority level of tasks through color saturation, with darker shades signifying higher importance. Actionable Tips for Implementation Start Simple: Begin with 3-4 main categories or colors to avoid overcomplication. Consistency is Key: Maintain a consistent color system across all your scheduling tools for seamless integration. Alternatives to Color: Consider using patterns or symbols as alternatives to colors for visual variety or accessibility considerations. Regular Review: Review your color balance weekly to ensure a healthy distribution of work and personal time, promoting work-life balance. Learn more about using color coding and visual systems . Why Use Visual Systems? For busy professionals constantly juggling multiple commitments, a clear and visually appealing schedule is essential. Color coding and visual systems transform a potentially overwhelming list of tasks into an easily digestible overview. This method not only improves time blocking efficiency but also contributes to better time management, reduced stress, and a clearer sense of control over your day. This technique is particularly valuable for visual learners and anyone seeking to optimize their workflow using tools like Sunsama. This strategy truly earns its spot on this list because it provides a powerful visual aid, facilitating better organization and a more balanced approach to time management. 6. Plan Your Blocks the Night Before One of the most effective time blocking tips is to plan your blocks the night before. This proactive approach sets the stage for a productive day by allowing you to allocate time for tasks strategically, minimizing decision fatigue in the morning. By completing your time blocking in the evening, you allow your subconscious to process the plan overnight, enabling you to start each day with clear direction and purpose. This eliminates the need to spend valuable morning energy on planning, allowing you to dive straight into your prioritized tasks. Examples of Planning the Night Before 15-Minute Evening Planning Sessions: Dedicate a short period each evening to review your schedule and block out time for the following day. This helps you visualize your day and ensures you're prepared. Sunday Evening Planning for the Entire Week: Take advantage of Sunday evenings to plan your entire week. This provides a bird's-eye view of your commitments and helps you proactively identify potential conflicts or areas for adjustment. End-of-Workday Planning for Tomorrow: Before leaving work, spend a few minutes outlining your schedule for the next day. This creates a seamless transition between workdays and ensures a productive start. Using Commute Time for Mental Planning: If you commute, leverage this time for mental planning. Mentally rehearse your schedule and consider potential time blocks for upcoming tasks. Actionable Tips for Implementation Keep Planning Sessions Short (10-15 minutes): Avoid lengthy planning sessions. Short, focused planning periods are more effective and sustainable. Review the Previous Day's Performance First: Before planning for the next day, briefly assess your performance from the current day. Identify any areas where you could improve your time management. Include Personal and Work Commitments: Integrate both personal appointments and work tasks into your time blocks to create a holistic view of your day. This helps maintain a work-life balance. Leave Some Flexibility for Morning Adjustments: While planning is essential, build in some flexibility for unexpected events or last-minute changes that may arise in the morning. Why Plan the Night Before? For busy professionals, particularly those in demanding roles like tech workers, consultants, entrepreneurs, and CEOs, planning the night before is invaluable. It provides a sense of control and reduces stress related to time management. This technique, popularized by historical figures like Benjamin Franklin with his daily planning rituals and modern productivity experts like Stephen Covey with his 7 Habits methodology, provides a framework for proactive scheduling. Planning your time blocks the night before deserves its place in this list because it sets a powerful precedent for maximizing productivity and minimizing wasted time. By incorporating this time blocking tip into your routine, you can approach each day with intention and achieve greater focus, making it a valuable asset for anyone seeking to optimize their workflow using tools like Sunsama. 7. Include Personal and Self-Care Blocks One of the most overlooked aspects of time blocking is incorporating personal appointments and self-care. Often, work tasks dominate our schedules, leaving little room for essential activities that contribute to our well-being. Deliberately scheduling time blocks for personal activities, exercise, meals, and self-care with the same priority as work tasks ensures a healthy work-life balance and prevents burnout. Treat these blocks as unmovable appointments, just like any important meeting. Examples of Personal and Self-Care Blocks Lunch Break: Block an hour for lunch each day, treating it as an essential meeting you cannot miss. Exercise: Schedule dedicated workout sessions, whether it's a morning run or an evening yoga class. Family Time: Protect family dinner time by blocking it off in your schedule and avoiding work intrusions. Personal Development: Allocate time for hobbies, reading, or learning new skills to nurture personal growth. Actionable Tips for Implementation Start with Non-Negotiables: Begin by blocking off non-negotiable personal commitments, such as doctor's appointments or family events. Communicate Boundaries: Clearly communicate your personal time blocks to colleagues to minimize interruptions and maintain boundaries. Unified Calendar: Use the same calendar for both work and personal appointments to get a holistic view of your schedule and avoid conflicts. Serious Commitment: Treat personal appointments with the same level of seriousness as business meetings, avoiding rescheduling or canceling them unless absolutely necessary. Why Include Personal and Self-Care Blocks? For busy professionals, particularly tech workers, consultants, entrepreneurs, and CEOs, maintaining a healthy work-life integration is crucial for sustained productivity and overall well-being. Learn more about tips for work-life balance . Time blocking for personal activities isn't just about having fun; it's a strategic investment in your physical and mental health. By prioritizing personal time, you reduce stress, improve focus, and increase your overall effectiveness in both your professional and personal life. This approach is especially valuable for those prone to overworking or struggling to disconnect from work. Incorporating personal and self-care blocks deserves a place in this list because it provides a practical framework for protecting your well-being while maximizing your productivity using time blocking tools like Sunsama. It acknowledges that true productivity comes from a balanced life, not just a packed schedule. 8. Review and Adjust Weekly One of the most overlooked aspects of successful time blocking is the regular review and adjustment process. Just like any system, time blocking requires fine-tuning to maximize its effectiveness. A weekly review provides the opportunity to analyze what worked well, what didn't, and identify areas for improvement. This iterative approach allows you to adapt your time blocking system to your evolving needs and circumstances, ensuring it remains a valuable tool for productivity. Examples of Weekly Reviews Friday Afternoon Review: Dedicate 30 minutes every Friday afternoon to reflect on the past week's schedule. Monthly Deep Dive: Conduct a more in-depth monthly analysis of your time blocking data to identify larger trends and patterns. Project-Based Adjustments: Review your time blocks after completing a significant project to assess efficiency and make adjustments for future projects. Actionable Tips for Implementation Schedule It: Block time on your calendar for your weekly review, making it a non-negotiable part of your routine. Track Metrics: Monitor key metrics such as task completion rates and the accuracy of your time estimates. Reflect on Energy Levels: Consider what activities energized you and which ones drained you. This can inform future scheduling decisions. Incremental Changes: Make small, targeted adjustments to your time blocks rather than drastic overhauls. Why Review and Adjust? For busy professionals like tech workers, consultants, and entrepreneurs, time is a finite resource. Time blocking offers a structured approach to managing that resource effectively. However, without regular review and adjustment, your time blocks can become rigid and fail to reflect your current priorities. Learn more about how to conduct effective reviews in this helpful guide: How to Conduct a Weekly Review to Do More of the Right Things . A weekly review allows you to adapt to changing demands, optimize your schedule, and ensure your time blocking system remains aligned with your goals. This ongoing process of refinement is crucial for maximizing the long-term benefits of time blocking and deserves its place in this list of essential time blocking tips. It empowers you to stay flexible, adapt to change, and continuously improve your time management skills. This approach is particularly beneficial when using tools like Sunsama, which facilitate detailed scheduling and tracking. Elevating Your Productivity with Sunsama and Time Blocking This curated collection of time blocking tips offers a powerful framework for ambitious professionals seeking to optimize their daily workflow. From starting small and batching similar tasks to strategically aligning tasks with energy levels and incorporating personal time, these strategies provide a holistic approach to productivity. Remember, effective time blocking isn't just about scheduling every minute; it's about intentionally designing your day to maximize focus and achieve meaningful results. Key Takeaways for Time Blocking Success Let's recap the most impactful takeaways from these time blocking tips: Intentional Planning: Proactive planning, ideally the night before, sets the stage for a productive day. This allows you to approach your work with purpose and minimizes decision fatigue. Flexibility and Adaptation: While structure is essential, building buffer time allows for unexpected interruptions and ensures your schedule remains realistic and adaptable. Regular review and adjustment are also crucial for long-term success. Personalization: Time blocking isn't one-size-fits-all. Experiment with different techniques like color-coding and find what resonates best with your individual working style. Prioritizing personal and self-care blocks ensures a sustainable approach to productivity. Putting Time Blocking into Action Mastering these time blocking tips can significantly enhance your productivity, reduce stress, and create a more balanced work life. By proactively managing your time, you gain control over your schedule, rather than letting it control you. This empowers you to focus on high-impact tasks, minimize distractions, and achieve your most ambitious goals. Start Small: Don't try to overhaul your entire schedule overnight. Begin by implementing one or two time blocking tips and gradually incorporate more as you become comfortable. Consistent Review: Regularly assess your time blocking strategy. What's working? What needs adjustment? This iterative process will help you refine your approach and maximize its effectiveness. Embrace the Power of Tools: Leverage technology to streamline your time blocking efforts. Sunsama, for example, offers a robust platform to implement these tips seamlessly. Transform Your Workflow with Sunsama Sunsama offers a purpose-built platform for implementing these time blocking tips. It integrates seamlessly with your existing calendar and task management tools, allowing you to visualize your day, schedule tasks effectively, and track your progress. Ready to experience the transformative power of intentional time management? Explore Sunsama today and unlock your full productivity potential.

title: May 2025 Company Update
summary: As we close out another month of Terran R development, we’re sharing a look at recent progress across design, build, test, and launch.   Design   In May, we completed an additional 17 component-level critical design reviews (CDR). At this stage of the program, many of th
body_text: As we close out another month of Terran R development, we’re sharing a look at recent progress across design, build, test, and launch. Design In May, we completed an additional 17 component-level critical design reviews (CDR). At this stage of the program, many of the releases are for less complex parts including trays, brackets, and manifolds. These designs are essential to supporting larger assemblies and we’re working to complete them in parallel with thrust structure build. Build Production efforts continue to ramp as we advance towards first flight. We used automated drilling to process thousands of holes on the thrust structure panels, an important step in accelerating production. The LOX dome was successfully loaded onto the circumferential friction stir welder (CFSW) in preparation for its second weld, and the stage 2 transfer tube is being welded, bringing us closer to completing the second stage tank. In parallel, hardware for the avionics hub, the network and low power distribution system for Terran R, has been released and is now being built. Across the factory, new manufacturing infrastructure continues to come online. We completed automated phased array ultrasonic testing (PAUT) inspection of the first flight circumferential weld, with a second automated PAUT being installed to support stringer inspection on the vertical friction stir welder. The newly installed vertical turning lathe will complete multi-axis work on domes, and a new horizontal friction stir welder is being installed, which will lap weld structural stringers onto Terran R’s first stage panels. As we continue to execute and scale Terran R production, we’ve brought on Robin Petitprez as Senior Vice President of Manufacturing and Supply Chain. Robin brings over a decade of hands-on experience in rapidly industrializing advanced aerospace and automotive systems at scale, and we are incredibly excited to welcome him to Relativity. Test Engine qualification is officially underway – a major milestone in the Terran R program. The Aeon R qualification unit was manufactured at our Long Beach headquarters and shipped to NASA Stennis, where it has since been activated. The campaign started strong with 11 hot fires and a new internal record of 4 hot fires in under 10 working hours. Engine qualification is critical for demonstrating performance and reliability ahead of flight. Propulsion is often one of the longest lead items in rocket development programs, so we’re proud to say that we’re tracking well and expect to wrap up the engine qualification campaign later this summer. Back in Long Beach, test efforts continue across the program. The team recently completed proof testing of the composite overwrapped pressure vessel (COPV) manifold assembly, validating structural integrity and leak-tightness. On the structural test stand, strut assemblies have been installed to simulate engine loads during upcoming tests. Valve qualification is also progressing, including testing on our in-house shock stand. Looking ahead, we’re already performing development tests for future engine block valve upgrades. We recently completed successful cure and non-destructive testing of our first development panels for the raceway covers. The composite panel, which is representative of the production covers, is now being tested to verify mechanical strength properties and quality. Launch Progress continues at LC-16, our launch site at Cape Canaveral. Work on the horizontal integration facility is underway, foundation installation for the water tower has begun, and the east flume wall of the diverter pit is now complete. As we continue progressing toward Terran R’s first flight, each milestone contributes to a broader objective: establishing the foundation for a scalable, efficient, and repeatable production system. This is a critical step in building the long-term production backbone required to support a high-cadence, commercially viable launch program.
